definition: MISO 47 steam-gas overnight + CT evening drag keeper candidate: miso-46 seam-ladder recipe re-solved at HEAD, absorbing two base-data structural mechanisms vs miso-46 — (1) ST_GAS extreme-day overnight [0,6] drag in the reliability_floor engine (tmax/tmin/netload, min-stable 0.12, 4 limbs enabled where the CAMPD overnight pre-positioning is real, forced 0.7-1.2% in-solve), (2) CT_PEAKER evening [15,21] netload drag replacing the temperature-only CT limbs (6 zones, rho 0.49-0.71, forced 5.0-7.5% in-solve — under the 15% peaker cap; D-1/D-2/D-4 all pass). The MISO CHP steam-credit HR correction was audited and LEFT OFF (MISO CHP does not over-deliver). Recipe byte-unchanged vs miso-46; every delta is one of these two drag mechanisms in reliability_floor_coeffs_MISO.csv.
market_story: CT_PEAKER: MISO commits simple-cycle peakers for local Resource Adequacy through the afternoon-evening net-load ramp (the duck-neck: cooling load climbs while solar collapses at sunset); the evening [15,21] net-load floor reproduces that committed evening SHAPE the energy-only LP decommits (D-1 diurnal r~0.99, forced 5-7.5% under the peaker budget). ST_GAS: legacy gas-steam boilers are held warm at physical min-stable (0.12) through the overnight [0,6] trough on extreme-temperature / high-net-load days to ramp for the NEXT peak rather than pay a multi-hour cold start (forced 0.7-1.2%). Both are commitment scaffolding, not volume levers - the residual CT/ST_GAS annual under-run is a separate merit-position model miss (disclosed), not what the floor buys.
